text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: GPU_INFERENCE_OOM on prod-cluster-4 (service: inference-gpu-pool)

jamie: acked. I'm on call. seeing spikes in OOM errors across nodes in az-us-west-2a.

sasha: looking at metrics now — GPU mem usage jumping to ~98% on a subset of pods, tensor cache growth on long-running chats. Tail lat spikes reported by console routes /v1/chat.

omar: any customer-facing errors? PD summary said 12% error rate on requests to model: redwood/ggml-7b-v1, increased latency ~800ms.

jamie: yes, some 5xxs (CUDA OOM) and buffer-alloc failures. Rolling counts: ~230 OOMs in last 10m. Marking impact: partial degraded for hosted.

pagerduty-bot: Escalation policy: oncall -> oncall-2 after 3m if unacknowledged. Acknowledged by jamie.

sasha: grabbing kube logs from one failing pod:
```
E tensorflow: cudart.cpp:292 cudaCheckStatus() failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/runner.py", line 412, in handle_request
    ctx.iterate()
  File "/app/ctx.py", line 88, in iterate
    self.kv_cache.extend(new_kv)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory when allocating 1.3 GiB (kernel: nv_add)
```

jamie: sounds like KV cache growth from long chats plus aggressive batching. Quick mitigations: 1) reduce max_batch_size for the model route, 2) restart the most afflicted pods, 3) enable fallback to CPU-small variant for new requests.

mira: I can toggle a routing policy to send traffic to cpu-fallback group. Do you want me to flip it?

jamie: yes, do cpu-fallback for all non-priority traffic. Also set route-level max_input_tokens=2048 and max_batch=4.

sasha: running k8s drain+restart on pod inference-ggml-47: `kubectl -n prod scale deployment inference-ggml --replicas=0 && sleep 8 && kubectl scale deployment inference-ggml --replicas=4`

omar: I'll cordon node ip-10-2-7-88 and evacuate workloads. Node GPU mem pressure showing steady growth even after restarts — might be a memory leak in the runtime when handling long KV sequences.

jamie: also reduce runtime cache retention: set ENV KV_CACHE_TTL=600 for the deployment to drop stale caches faster.

sasha: patched and redeployed a configmap with new envs. Restarting pods. Watch logs.

(2m later)

sasha: after restarts and routing change, OOMs dropped to 5 in last 5m. Latency back to baseline ~120ms for most routes.

omar: still seeing one node with high GPU reserved memory. Investigating driver/kernel mismatch — I saw a few `cuCtxCreate` warnings earlier.

jamie: if driver mismatch, open a maintenance ticket with infra. For now continue draining that node.

pagerduty-bot: note: incident acknowledged by jamie at 1782003460, escalations paused.

mira: routing switch applied. CPU fallback handling ~30% of traffic now. No big customer complaints on support channels as of now.

sasha: adding temporary guardrails into runtime to cap per-request KV tokens to 12k. Patch pushed.

(15m later)

jamie: propose transitioning to mitigation->monitoring phase. OOMs under control. I'll hand off to sasha for postmortem and long-term fix.

sasha: taking handoff. I'll open an incident issue with hypothesis: KV cache growth + batching + a regression in kernel memory reclamation. Actions to track: reproduce with long chat workloads, add unit tests for KV GC, audit recent runtime memory changes, coordinate driver/OS patching with infra.

omar: leaving node cordoned until driver validated. If any remaining 5xxs spike, notify oncall immediately.

jamie: thanks team. Marking thread resolved in PD once postmortem ticket exists. :white_check_mark:

sasha: creating ticket INF-2026 and assigning owners. Will include timeline, logs, and config diffs.

mira: ping me if you need a traffic rollback.

incident-bot: Incident thread closed by jamie at 1782003789.
